They weigh exactly the same — one kilogram is one kilogram, regardless of the material.

This is a classic trick question! The intuitive (but wrong) answer is "steel," because steel is much *denser* than feathers. Density is mass per unit volume, so a kilogram of steel would be a small, compact block, while a kilogram of feathers would be a huge, fluffy pile. But on a scale, both would read exactly 1 kg.
